evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs on pull_request, runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in site/. All of these exist in site/package.json; build includes svelte-check. Permissions: `contents: read` in ci.yml; in pages.yml, read at the top and `pages: write`/`id-token: write` only on the deploy job; `contents: write` in release.yml. Only github.token is used, there is no pull_request_target, and nothing was pushed or run. The problem: every action is a mutable tag, not a full commit SHA (`actions/checkout@v4`, `setup-node@v4`, `upload-pages-artifact@v3`, `deploy-pages@v4`; step1.patch lines 53-54, 93-94, 105, 121, 146-147). Also, pages.yml allows `workflow_dispatch` with no `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` guard, so the workflow alone does not stop a deploy from another branch; only the github-pages environment's default branch policy would. release.yml's write token is also present during `npm ci`/`npm test`.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch lines 313-382) covers requirements, install (`cd site; npm ci`), develop (`npm run dev`), test, build/preview, the other scripts (index, fieldsets, prepare-data, sample-bullets), PAGES_BASE (vite.config.ts:11 reads it), contributing (data steps linked to CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-data, issue forms, commit convention), releases and license (LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY.md exist). Every command exists in site/package.json. Referenced paths exist: fixtures/, data/bullets/README.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.
evidence.s1_release: One strategy, used consistently: the version lives in site/package.json (0.1.0); SemVer rules are in CONTRIBUTING.md#versioning; the release is a tag-triggered workflow that checks the tag against package.json, extracts the CHANGELOG section as notes and attaches the built site; CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and has an Unreleased section; Dependabot covers npm in /site and github-actions. The commit convention (Conventional Commits) is stated, and all 7 commits follow it. One inconsistency: dependabot.yml sets the npm commit prefix to `chore`, but CONTRIBUTING's type table assigns dependencies to `build` (and the agent's own Dependabot commit uses `build:`).
evidence.s2_requirements: Every requirement is met. Route `#/compare/<a>/<b>` is parsed from location.hash, so it survives a reload (router.ts parse plus `href.compare`). The SVG has role=img and aria-label `t('compare.profiles')` = 'Profiles of {a} and {b}', with two `<path>` elements. Caption is 'Dimensions (mm|in)'. Headers are Symbol / A name / B name / Difference. The symbol comes from FIELD_LABELS; rows are cartridge-part numbers without a FIELD_UNITS entry and without Tol fields; difference is B−A. Values follow the unitSystem() preference. Cartridge.svelte has a labelled `Compare with` NativeSelect and a `Compare` button that goes to href.compare(key, chosen). German strings are given for every key. Shot cartridges are excluded from the select and rejected in the view, which the scope allows.
evidence.s2_correctness: compare.ts: metric values use formatValue (e.g. '1.4', '0.94', '51.18'); imperial values use displayNumber(mm,'in'); differences are taken in mm and written with displayNumber, which removes float noise (e min: 0.94−1.4 → '-0.46'; L3: '15.37'). Both profiles come from caseOuterProfile(adaptMetallic(...)) and are drawn on one viewportFor([...]) with frame 'landscape', so they share the scale, the axis and z=0 (the head face); a test checks this. A record that cannot be drawn returns null and shows a message. Unknown keys or shotshells reject the promise and reach the {:catch} message. Checked against data/cartridges/rimless/308_win.json and belted/300_win_mag.json.
evidence.s2_fit: It reuses lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath, fmt), lib/shapes2d (caseOuterProfile, adaptMetallic), site units.ts/units.svelte.ts, PageHeader, NativeSelect, Label, ShadcnButton, the lazy chunk pattern in App.svelte, metadata.ts and the nav active state. The rest is idiomatic. One small duplication: compare.ts:152 reimplements the group ordering of site/src/lib/fields.ts `orderedGroups` (without its sort of unknown groups). The touched files are limited to what the feature needs.
evidence.s2_tests: site/src/lib/compare.test.ts tests real data (308 Win / 300 Win Mag) with Vitest: symbol labels ('e min', 'L3 + G'), unique rows, exclusion of tolerances/angles/non-mm fields, B−A without float noise, intersection behaviour, imperial conversion, two paths sharing head-face x and axis y, and the null case. router.test.ts covers route parsing, encoding round-trips and malformed hashes. Missing: nothing tests the caption/unit label, the headers/accessible name, or the detail-page select. The repository has no component-test setup, so pure-function tests fit its setup. The imperial test compares against displayNumber itself, which is partly tautological.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: compareRows (step3.patch lines 43-57) now takes the union of both symbol sets and leaves the empty cell and Difference blank where a cartridge does not publish a symbol. The test now checks 'delta L' (A only), 'R3' (B only) and that 'Fe' still has a difference. Style: step 2 had already given the three numeric columns and their headers `text-right` (step2.patch lines 418-429), and Tailwind utilities sit above the legacy layer (shadcn.css:1), so no change was needed and none was made; nothing unrelated was touched. Minor: B-only symbols are added after all of A's rows (R3 comes after misc rather than in its caseHead position).
evidence.cross_step: Both steps added entries under CHANGELOG `## [Unreleased]` / Added, and step 3 amended the entry for the unreleased feature. The strategy bumps the version only at release time, so leaving 0.1.0 unchanged is consistent. The commits `feat: compare two cartridges at #/compare/<a>/<b>` and `fix: list dimensions that only one cartridge publishes in the compare table` follow Conventional Commits. I did not run the checks; from reading the code they look type-safe and should pass: Promise.all returns a tuple, so `[first, second]` destructures cleanly, and the `compareKey` const keeps its narrowing inside {#if}. The new tests use the existing Vitest include.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 / CI criterion: actions are pinned to mutable version tags (@v4/@v3), not full commit SHAs, in ci.yml, pages.yml and release.yml
strengths: The compare logic in compare.ts is small and correct. It reuses lib/core field metadata, formatValue, lib/geom viewportFor/fullSectionPath and lib/shapes2d caseOuterProfile instead of duplicating geometry or formatting.

The release setup is coherent: a tag-triggered workflow checks the tag against site/package.json, publishes that version's Keep a Changelog section as the notes, and is documented step by step in CONTRIBUTING.md.
The README and CONTRIBUTING show only commands that exist, cover data contribution and licensing, and every commit across the three steps follows the stated Conventional Commits convention.
issues: None of the GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs (actions/checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, upload-pages-artifact@v3, deploy-pages@v4).
pages.yml accepts workflow_dispatch with no branch guard, and release.yml grants contents: write to the whole job, including npm ci/test.

Small inconsistencies: dependabot.yml uses the `chore` prefix for npm, though the convention assigns dependencies to `build`; compare.ts re-implements orderedGroups' group ordering; B-only rows are added at the end of the table rather than in sheet order.
review.verdict: The compare feature and the step 3 fix are correct, follow the repository's style, are reasonably tested, and follow the changelog and commit conventions set up in step 1. The main thing holding back a merge is CI hardening: unpinned actions, and a Pages workflow that can be dispatched from any branch.
